.engine/operations/boot-session-start.md.why: boot-session-start is the heaviest member of the orientation family — the SessionStart pack a cold session is meant to read in full, every boot. Its length is load-bearing operator-facing content: the anti-habituation collapse rules and the repair-offer contracts in Notes, each a real behavior carrying its own tool name, loss semantics, and issue/decision reference, none redundant with another. When the 150 ceiling was set the repair set held five contracts (un-stranding, catch-up, off-main return, stranded-pull-request reconcile, branch-protection re-enable) at 121 body lines; it has since grown to ten — adding fresh-copy setup (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#353), engine-mechanic product-checkout orientation (eADR-0026), half-finished-upgrade finish/undo (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#594), leftover-template-license clear/keep (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#471), and greenfield-intake offer/dismiss (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#553). That is genuine capability growth, not the repetition issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#364 trimmed. This session first trimmed the real over-narration — the per-bullet restatements of the shared repair-offer preamble, a duplicated read-only-of-canonical-state refinement, and the anti-habituation prose — landing the file at 184 body lines, then raised the ceiling to 200 for the load-bearing remainder. The 200 ceiling is the operator's deliberate choice, set with durable headroom so the next repair contract does not force another guarded edit in a later session. It is still a ceiling, not a removal: the soft nudge fires again above 200, and this rule's hard tier still fails a malformed or reasonless override, so a dead grant cannot silently accumulate. The raise lives in this guarded rule, so it needs the operator's deliberate sign-off — the recorded-reason pattern issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#273 asked for, and the resolution of issue StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#460 (a recorded ceiling rather than a runbook silently sitting over budget, or its load-bearing prose shaved to fit).

.engine/operations/build-orchestration.m.why: build-orchestration remains the convergence runbook for planning, review, implementation, validation, repair, and submission, but the mechanical Build coordinator now carries repeatable state and evidence handling that previously required extensive procedural narration here. The reconstructed runbook is 221 prose-body lines: the 120-line default would still crowd its responsibility boundary, plan-storage rules, two review gates, proportional repair judgment, and human merge gate, while 250 leaves modest headroom without preserving the obsolete 450-line grant sized for the former 392-line procedure. This is the operator's deliberate post-reconstruction ceiling choice; the soft nudge fires above 250 and the rule's hard tier still rejects a malformed or reasonless override.

message: An operation (a runbook under .engine/operations/) must contain, as level-2 headings in this order, Purpose, then Steps, then Done when, and it may also contain a Notes section, and no others. These sections are what make a runbook followable — what it is for, the ordered steps, and how to know it is done — so an operation that omits a required one is structurally incomplete. This check catches a broken SHAPE only: that the required sections are present, correctly ordered, and that no stray section appears. It cannot judge whether a section's content is substantive — an empty or hand-wavy section passes here and is caught instead by the operator reviewing the committed change, and whether the runbook actually tells a cold operator how to perform the procedure is the audits layer's judgment, not this check's. Length over an operation's line budget is only a soft nudge to trim, never a block; the budget is 120 by default, and a specific operation may carry a higher recorded budget in length_budget_overrides. A malformed or stale override entry — one missing its budget or recorded reason, or naming no operation — is the rule's hard tier, so a dead budget grant cannot accumulate. Add or reorder the flagged sections to match the operation template (.engine/templates/operation.md) before merging.
